Definition: to gather for any purpose; hence, to receive, take away, i.e. remove (destroy, leave behind, put up, restore, etc.)
BiblicalUsage: This is the everyday verb for gathering — to collect, to take in, to take away. Rachel says 'God hath taken away my reproach' when Joseph is born; Moses tells Pharaoh to 'gather thy cattle' before the hail; and the people 'gathered the quails' all day and all night in the wilderness.
TheologicalSignificance: The same word gathers a reproach away, gathers cattle from the field, and gathers quails for a hungry camp — God gathers and God takes away. I believe the word is a small picture of His providence: He gathers what we need, and He takes away what shames us, and both are His work.
